examples.result: The skill runs `show release-checklist` and prints the document that answers the name. It reads nothing from tier folders itself.

examples.prompt: Which references exist, and which copy of each is used?
examples.result: The skill runs `list` and reports every layer it read, then each reference with the copy marked `used` and the ones marked `shadowed`.

examples.prompt: Find a reference about commit messages.
examples.result: The skill runs `search` with the topic and names the best matches. When nothing matches it says so and does not guess a name.

examples.prompt: Create a project reference called release-checklist.
examples.result: The skill runs `create release-checklist --dry-run`, shows you the target path and the content, and writes the file under `.agents/references/` only after you approve. It then runs `show release-checklist --trace` and confirms the new file is `used`.

examples.prompt: Change what the commit-style reference says, just for me.
examples.result: The skill writes an override in `~/.agents/references/` marked `merge-sections`, so the sections you do not redefine are kept. It never edits a copy a plugin ships.

examples.prompt: Delete my project copy of release-checklist.
examples.result: The skill runs `delete release-checklist --dry-run`, shows the file and what answers the name afterwards, and deletes only after you approve.

examples.prompt: Why does commit-style resolve to that file?
examples.result: The skill runs `show commit-style --trace` and reports the layer that was `used` and each layer that was `shadowed` or `not read`, with its reason.

cli.$run:
Install the package, or run it once with `npx`. The `reference` skill runs the same command from a launcher bundled in the plugin.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @cyberuni/agent-harness
npx agent-harness reference list

# or, without installing
npx -y @cyberuni/agent-harness reference list
```
cli.$format: `show`, `create`, and `delete` answer in `text` unless `--format` says otherwise. The other subcommands answer in `toon`, a compact format an agent reads. Pass `--format json` to pipe the answer. Errors go to stderr, so stdout carries only the answer.

examples.explain: The document prints as it is, without frontmatter.

examples.title: Report why a name resolved to one copy.
examples.explain: `--trace` adds every path checked, the file that matched, the merge mode, and why a layer was dropped. It goes to stderr in `text` format, so this page shows only the document; run it to see the trace.

examples.explain: `*` stands for any run of characters; the rest must match exactly.

examples.explain: Slots are listed highest precedence first.
